name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean of D+11
Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with $1.2M cash on hand
Challenger Dennis Hannon has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Kennedy at ~96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: a D+11 district, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge against a challenger with no reported money. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much tighter race or a surge of outside spending for Hannon would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent in this Buffalo-area district, is seeking another term after winning the seat in a special election. The district leans Democratic by about 11 points, and Kennedy has built a substantial financial advantage, raising $2.3 million and holding $1.2 million on hand. Republican challenger Dennis Hannon reports no fundraising, and no outside groups have engaged in the race.

No public general-election polling exists, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Kennedy roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. With a strong partisan lean, an entrenched incumbent, and a large money gap, this race sits firmly in the Safe Democratic category, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling.
